title: Given an unsorted integer array, find the length of the longest run of consecutive integers. The numbers may appear in any order, and the algorithm must run in linear time.
shortTitle: Longest Consecutive Sequence: HashSet, Expand Each Potential Start
keyPoints: Put all numbers in a HashSet for O(1) membership checks; the set also deduplicates automatically.
Only start counting from a number whose predecessor (value minus one) is absent in the set.
From each true start, expand forward counting consecutive successors until the chain breaks.
Total time is O(n) because each number is visited at most twice: once in the outer scan and once in an inner expansion.
The start-only guard is what makes it linear, not quadratic, despite the nested loop appearance.
Sorting would also find the answer but in O(n log n); the HashSet approach avoids sorting entirely.

s1_definition.oneliner: Put everything in a set, start counting only from numbers whose predecessor is absent, and expand forward.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Longest Consecutive Sequence** – find the length of the longest run of consecutive integers in an unsorted array.
- **HashSet** – provides O(1) membership checks and automatic deduplication.
- **True start** – a number whose predecessor (value minus one) is not in the set; only true starts begin an expansion.
- **Forward expansion** – from a true start, count how many consecutive successors are present.
- **Time** – O(n) because each number is touched at most twice across all expansions.
- **Space** – O(n) for the set.
s1_definition.analogy: The bank has a jumbled pile of cheque serial numbers and wants the longest unbroken run of consecutive numbers. A clerk dumps them all into a fast lookup box. Then for each number the clerk checks: is the number one less than me also in the box? If yes, I am in the middle of a run, skip me. If no, I am the start of a run, so the clerk counts upward until the chain breaks.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Input: [100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2]
  Set:   {100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2}

  Scan each number:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ num=100: has 99? NO  --> true start          │
  │   expand: 100, 101? NO  --> length=1         │
  │                                              │
  │ num=4:   has 3?  YES --> skip (middle of run)│
  │                                              │
  │ num=200: has 199? NO --> true start           │
  │   expand: 200, 201? NO  --> length=1         │
  │                                              │
  │ num=1:   has 0?  NO  --> true start          │
  │   expand: 1, 2? YES, 3? YES, 4? YES, 5? NO  │
  │   length=4  <-- LONGEST                      │
  │                                              │
  │ num=3:   has 2?  YES --> skip                │
  │ num=2:   has 1?  YES --> skip                │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Result: 4 (sequence [1, 2, 3, 4])
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Finding the longest run of consecutive integers in an unsorted array in linear time comes down to two ideas: a HashSet for O(1) membership checks, and the discipline of only beginning to count from a number that is a genuine start. A number is a genuine start when the value one less than it is not in the set, because if its predecessor were present it would be somewhere in the middle of a longer run.

The part that trips people up is the time complexity. It looks like a loop inside a loop, which suggests quadratic, but the start-only guard guarantees that the inner expansion runs only once per run and visits each number exactly once across the whole execution. Every element is touched at most twice, once by the outer scan and once by a single inner expansion, which makes the total linear.

In my banking project at the National Bank of India, cheque serial numbers arrive unsorted from batch processing, and the fraud team wants the longest run of consecutive serials in a batch because a very long consecutive block can signal a bulk-issued set worth reviewing. This method finds it without sorting, which matters because sorting a large real-time batch would add an O(n log n) cost we want to avoid.

Two practical benefits are that the HashSet deduplicates automatically, so reprocessed duplicate serials do not inflate the run length, and gaps between serial blocks are handled naturally because the forward expansion stops at the first missing successor.

Remember one sentence: put all values in a HashSet, only start counting from numbers whose predecessor is absent, and expand forward for O(n) longest consecutive sequence detection.
